journal.title: American journal of ophthalmology case reports

result.abstractText:
Purpose

The purpose of this case report is to describe a rare case of retained orbital brachytherapy seeds implanted during infancy and identified in an older adult undergoing neurocognitive evaluation. It highlights a multidisciplinary approach to diagnosis and management.

Observations

An 85-year-old man presented for removal of radiopaque periocular foreign bodies prior to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for a neurocognitive workup. The patient reported undergoing "seed placement" radiation therapy to the right orbital region at 18 months of age in Scotland for a superior right orbital mass, suspected to be a capillary hemangioma. Computed tomography revealed two discrete radiopaque foreign bodies in the superior right orbit and right medial nasal soft tissue. Multidisciplinary evaluation with ocular oncology and radiation safety suggested that the foreign bodies were retained casings from historical radon-222 brachytherapy seeds. Preoperative and intraoperative assessments demonstrated no detectable residual radioactivity, and the foreign bodies were removed successfully, allowing the patient to proceed with MRI.

Conclusions and importance

This case highlights the importance of recognizing historical radiation treatments as potential causes of orbital foreign bodies and imaging artifacts in older adult patients. It also underscores the value of multidisciplinary management for the safety of patients.
